description:
## Background

The planned `mise run gate` includes Rust formatting checks and Clippy with warnings treated as errors. The current repository cannot adopt those checks unchanged because the baseline is already red: `cargo fmt --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml -- --check` reports formatting differences in tracked Rust files, and `cargo clippy --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml -- -D warnings` reports seven warnings. `cargo test` passes but emits two test-only warnings.

The gate should expose new regressions, not fail solely because the repository has never satisfied its proposed strict policy.

## What to build

Bring the tracked Rust backend to a clean baseline suitable for strict automated gates without changing runtime behavior, the TauRPC contract, or test intent.

## Technical Approach

- Run Rust formatting and apply only the resulting formatting changes.
- Resolve the current Clippy findings, including complex type signatures, argument-count structure, collapsible conditionals, derivable defaults, and redundant pattern matching.
- Decide whether test targets are included in the Clippy policy. The default is `cargo clippy --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml --all-targets -- -D warnings`.
- Resolve test-only warnings where they are genuine dead code, or document a narrowly scoped exception if a warning is intentionally required.
- Keep changes limited to the Rust baseline and avoid combining unrelated refactors.

## Considerations

- Preserve all existing behavior and test assertions.
- Do not broaden production visibility merely to silence a warning.
- The selected Rust toolchain must be the one later pinned by mise: Rust 1.97.1 with rustfmt and Clippy available.
- If strict Clippy requires broad architectural changes, stop and report the affected findings rather than silently weakening the policy.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `cargo fmt --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml -- --check` exits 0.
- [ ] `cargo clippy --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml --all-targets -- -D warnings` exits 0, or a separately tracked and explicitly approved exception documents why it cannot yet do so.
- [ ] `cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml` passes with no newly introduced warnings.
- [ ] Rust runtime behavior, public contracts, and test coverage are unchanged.
- [ ] The final diff contains only baseline formatting, warning fixes, and necessary focused tests/comments.

## Test Plan

- Run focused tests for every touched module.
- Run `cargo fmt --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml -- --check`.
- Run `cargo clippy --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml --all-targets -- -D warnings`.
- Run `cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml`.

## Triage
